children: , a leading biopharmaceutical company focused on revolutionizing medicine leveraging CRISPR gene editing and other core technologies, today announced the appointment of Jing L. Marantz, M.D., Ph.D., as Executive Vice President and Chief Medical Officer, effective October 26, 2026. Dr. Marantz is an accomplished drug development leader with more than 25 years of experience in the biopharmaceutical industry that includes the successful advancement of several now-approved rare disease therapies. In this role, Dr. Marantz will lead the company’s translational, development, regulatory and medical affairs functions.

“Jing is an exceptional leader with a track record of success in the rare disease space across the full lifecycle from development through regulatory approval and commercialization,” said John Leonard, M.D., Intellia President and Chief Executive Officer. “We are delighted to welcome her as our Chief Medical Officer during this exciting and momentous time at Intellia. Her unique combination of development and business experience will be critical for our next phase as we seek to commercialize our first potential
gene editing product, advance our Phase 3 clinical trials in transthyretin amyloidosis and further expand our pipeline.”

“I am thrilled to join Intellia, where we have the opportunity to profoundly improve patient lives by delivering durable efficacy while minimizing treatment burden leveraging Nobel-prize-winning science,” said Dr. Marantz. “I look forward to working with the company’s talented team to advance our clinical programs with the goal of bringing new therapeutic options to patients with serious diseases.”

Dr. Marantz’s leadership experience spans research and development, medical affairs, business development and portfolio strategy across multiple specialties and rare diseases. Most recently, she served as Chief Medical Officer for Scholar Rock, where she led the development organization in advancing multiple clinical programs across neuromuscular, oncology and obesity, culminating in the U.S. approval of ISEMBYLD, the first muscle-targeted therapy for Spinal Muscular Atrophy. During her tenure at Scholar Rock, Dr. Marantz led simultaneous regulatory submissions to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and European Medicines Agency followed by successful engagement with Japan’s Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency, achieving alignment for a Japanese New Drug Application submission without clinical trial data in Japanese patients.

Prior to her role at Scholar Rock, Dr. Marantz held senior leadership positions at Krystal Biotech, Acceleron, Alnylam, Alexion, Biogen, ARIAD and Millennium Pharmaceuticals, playing key roles in the development and commercialization of over a dozen products across hematology/oncology, neurology and rare diseases. She is a member of the Board of Directors for Arcturus Therapeutics, Inc. Dr. Marantz received her medical training from Tongji Medical College, a Ph.D. in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology from the Medical University of South Carolina, and an MBA from the University of California at Berkeley.
